excerpt: Truework verifies income and employment for mortgage lenders and others. Checkr agreed to acquire it in April 2025. What it does and alternatives.
content:
Truework is a US platform that verifies a person's income and employment. Lenders, especially mortgage lenders, use it when underwriting a loan, and property managers and employers use it for rental and hiring checks. Its website calls it a unified VOIEA platform (verification of income, employment and assets) and claims it can verify 97% of US workers faster and at up to 50% lower cost; those are the company's own figures.

Truework's selling point is that it brings several ways of verifying a worker's income and employment together behind one service, so a lender does not have to try each source separately. Checkr, which now owns it, described Truework as the first provider to connect every major verification method into one platform, and said it uses AI and automation to make underwriting simpler.

On 17 April 2025 Checkr, the background-check company, announced that it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire Truework, expected to close in the second quarter of 2025. Checkr said Truework had thousands of customers, from small businesses to large financial institutions, including eight of the top ten US lenders by origination volume, and that the deal took Checkr into employment verification, which it called a multi-billion dollar market. Axios reported that Truework had raised a little over $125 million and was last valued at around $480 million, according to PitchBook. Financial terms were not disclosed. Truework's site now describes itself as a Checkr company.

Truework does not publish prices for lenders; you book a demo. Individuals whose employment is being verified do not pay. The service is US-only.

This profile is put together from the company's own pages and published reporting, checked on 15 October 2026. We have not tested the product, and nothing here is paid placement.

alternatives.intro: Other products that do a similar job. We have not compared them hands-on; check each one's own site for current prices.

items.difference: The largest incumbent, built on employer-contributed payroll data.
